why: Cultural anthropologist Richard Kurin presents the strand of hair from Thomas Jefferson's Bible that launched a 15-year genomic investigation into Jefferson's paternity of Sally Hemings' children — an intersection of DNA science and American history.

name: Midterms: Are Free Elections at Risk? — Melissa Murray, Andrew Weissmann & Bob Bauer at NY Historical Society
venue: New York Historical Society (Robert H. Smith Auditorium)
why: Panel on legal issues surrounding American elections with legal scholars Melissa Murray, Andrew Weissmann, and Bob Bauer — part of the Bonnie and Richard Reiss Lecture on Constitutional History and Law, timed to midterm season.

name: Wiseman's New York: Public vs. Private — Closing Panel at Union Docs
why: Closing panel for Wiseman's New York screening series at Union Docs — Urban Omnibus Editor-in-Chief Mariana Mogilevich, critic K. Austin Collins, filmmaker Nilita Vachani, and scholar Genevieve Yue discuss Frederick Wiseman's films and the structures of public vs. private space.

name: Architecture, Planning, and International Law: Building Postcarbon Futures at Architectural League
why: Free in-person panel at the Architectural League on how architecture and planning intersect with international law in the pursuit of postcarbon futures. CEUs available.

name: Beaux Arts Ball 2026 at Architectural League
why: The Architectural League's annual Beaux Arts Ball — one of New York's premier architecture and design fundraising galas — returns on October 23. Theme and venue to be announced.

name: Climate Week NYC at NYBG: Nature Your City Talks + Keynote
price: Free grounds admission for Climate Week events
why: NYBG Climate Week NYC features a keynote by leading urban ecologist Dr. Timon McPhearson and a panel on how to 'Nature Your City' — creating climate-resilient, equitable cities through green infrastructure. Grounds admission free for Climate Week events.

name: NYBG 5K Fun Run at New York Botanical Garden
why: NYBG's second annual 5K Fun Run through 250 acres including the Thain Family Forest (one of NYC's largest old-growth forests), Steinhardt Maple Collection, and historic Stone Mill. Supports NYBG's climate and biodiversity work.

name: Machel Montano: Journey of a Soca King Exhibition at Brooklyn Public Library (thru Sep 12)
why: Free exhibition celebrating Machel Montano's lifelong contributions to soca music and Caribbean culture, with costumes, trophies, and vinyl records from his career. On view at BPL Central Library through September 12.

name: What Makes a Brooklyn Summer Unique? — Panel at Brooklyn Public Library
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library (Dweck Center)
why: Capstone panel of BPL's Summer Reading Closing Festival with Adreinne Waheed, Jazmine Hughes, and Khalif Tahir Thompson, moderated by Tembe Denton-Hurst, celebrating the distinctive culture of Brooklyn summers.

name: Machel Montano's Musical Collaborations at Brooklyn Public Library
why: Program exploring the musical collaborations of soca king Machel Montano, part of BPL's Journey of a Soca King exhibition programming.

name: Like Ah Boss Film Screening & Music on the Plaza at Brooklyn Public Library
why: Outdoor film screening of Like Ah Boss (a documentary on Machel Montano) plus live music on the Central Library plaza, part of the Journey of a Soca King exhibition programming.

name: 9/11: Reclaiming Ground Zero — Documentary Screening & Talkback at BPL
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library (Dweck Center)
why: Screening of the new documentary 9/11: Reclaiming Ground Zero with director Josh Sabey and panelists including Michael Kimmelman, on the city's post-9/11 rebuilding — screened Sept 10, one day before the 25th anniversary.

name: Colin Kaepernick in Conversation with Nikole Hannah-Jones at Brooklyn Public Library
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library (Grand Lobby)
why: National book launch for Colin Kaepernick's memoir The Perilous Fight — the Super Bowl quarterback and civil rights activist in conversation with Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Nikole Hannah-Jones at BPL Central Library.

name: Jesse Wegman & Alexis Coe on The Lost Founder at Center for Brooklyn History
why: Journalist Jesse Wegman presents his new biography of James Wilson — an overlooked Founding Father — in conversation with historian Alexis Coe at the Center for Brooklyn History.

name: Space Jam 30th Anniversary Screening at Fort Greene Park (Tonight!)
time: Shortly after sundown (arrive early to picnic)
why: 30th anniversary screening of Space Jam at Fort Greene Park — Michael Jordan, Bugs Bunny, and the Monstars under the Brooklyn stars. Part of Summer Movies in the Park presented by NewYork-Presbyterian and Rooftop Films. Tonight!

name: BK Loves MJ (Spike Lee Joint) at Fort Greene Park
why: Spike Lee's annual BK Loves MJ celebration returns to Fort Greene Park on Michael Jackson's birthday — seven hours of music by legendary DJ Spinna. A Brooklyn institution.

name: The Namesake 20th Anniversary Screening + Q&A with Jhumpa Lahiri, Mira Nair & Kal Penn
why: 20th anniversary outdoor screening of The Namesake — Mira Nair's adaptation of Jhumpa Lahiri's novel — followed by a live Q&A with author Lahiri, director Nair, and lead actor Kal Penn at Fort Greene Park.

name: Fort Greene Park Jazz Festival
venue: Fort Greene Park, Monument Plaza (West Wing)
why: Annual jazz festival in the shadow of the Prison Ship Martyrs Monument — live soulful performances on the Monument Plaza. Bring a picnic blanket and enjoy four hours of free outdoor jazz in one of Brooklyn's loveliest parks.

name: Black History & Culture Tour of Fort Greene — The Heart of Black Fort Greene (Fulton Street)
venue: Fort Greene Park (Dekalb Ave/Washington Park entrance)
why: Led by local historian Suzanne Spellen, this guided tour traces Fort Greene's deep roots in Black history and culture along the Fulton Street corridor — from the 1800s through today. Developed with BlackSpace, MoCADA, and the Weeksville Heritage Center.

name: The Fling at Fort Greene Park — FGPC Annual Fundraiser
why: FGPC's 25th anniversary Fling fundraiser under the stars at Monument Plaza — live music from Brooklyn Music School Faculty Ensemble, dancing with Saint James Joy, desserts from Swu Bakes and Candor Candy, and complimentary beer and wine. 21+, BYOB picnic.

name: America's 250th Anniversary Tour of Fort Greene
venue: Fort Greene Park (Dekalb Ave/Washington Park entrance)
why: Walking tour tracing Fort Greene's role in the American Revolution — the Battle of Brooklyn, the founding of the park, and the legacy of prison ship martyrs — presented by historians Natasha Fearon and Alexandra Stevens as part of Brooklyn 250.

name: Explorers Club Climate Week 2026
why: The Explorers Club's annual Climate Week NYC programming returns for September 21-25, 2026 — with world-class speakers and news from the frontlines of climate change. Details and registration to be announced.

name: NY Transit Museum Bus Festival 2026 at Brooklyn Bridge Park
venue: Brooklyn Bridge Park, Emily Warren Roebling Plaza
why: The NY Transit Museum's 29th annual Bus Festival celebrates their 50th anniversary — climb aboard vintage buses, meet the drivers who keep NYC moving, do a scavenger hunt in the Transit Museum app, and browse the pop-up store, all with the Manhattan skyline backdrop at Brooklyn Bridge Park.

name: Vinyl Nights Presents: Return to '76 at NY Transit Museum
why: The Transit Museum's 50th anniversary fundraiser transforms the station platform into a two-level dance party powered by the rich analog sound of vinyl — disco spins on the mezzanine, funk and hip-hop take over the platform below, as DJs spin the music of '76.

name: Nostalgia Ride: An Afternoon Ride to Green-Wood Cemetery
why: Ride a vintage subway train to Brooklyn's historic Green-Wood Cemetery for a guided tour of the stories of its permanent residents — famous actors, politicians, artists, and inventors from the Victorian era and beyond. Includes time to picnic on the grounds.

name: Nostalgia Ride: Fly Away Redbirds (Morning Session) at NY Transit Museum
why: Board the iconic Redbird subway cars — in service 1959-2003 — for a round-trip excursion to the Bronx and back, departing from the historic Old South Ferry station (closed to the public since 2017). A rare chance to ride the Redbirds and access a hidden station.

name: Nostalgia Ride: Fly Away Redbirds (Afternoon Session) at NY Transit Museum
why: Afternoon session of the Redbird Nostalgia Ride — board the legendary subway cars in service from 1959-2003 for a round-trip to the Bronx, departing from the historic Old South Ferry station that has been closed to the public since 2017.

name: NY Transit Museum Transit Walk: Downtown Brooklyn (Sep 5)
venue: Meeting point TBD; ends at NY Transit Museum, Court Street
why: Expert-guided walk tracing Downtown Brooklyn's transit history from early ferry landings through trolleys and elevated railways to the subway era, concluding inside the Museum's historic Court Street station. Also offered Oct 17 and Nov 21.

name: NY Transit Museum Transit Walk: Gowanus and Carroll Gardens (Sep 13)
why: Guided walk through Gowanus and Carroll Gardens tracing how industrialization and transit transformed these unique historic Brooklyn neighborhoods. Also offered Oct 18.

name: NY Transit Museum: Underground NYC — Subway 101 Guided Ride (Oct 9)
venue: New York City Subway (meeting point TBD)
why: Expert-guided subway ride uncovering the system's hidden history — old stations, art, architecture, and exclusive archival images. Perfect for NYC transit obsessives and curious newcomers. Also offered Oct 24 and Nov 12.

name: NY Transit Museum Transit Walk: Art & Design Secrets of Penn Station and Moynihan Train Hall (Oct 24)
venue: Penn Station / Moynihan Train Hall (meeting point TBD)
why: Deep-dive tour of Penn Station's hidden Beaux-Arts architectural remnants and Moynihan Train Hall's new public artworks — tracing the story from the station's 1910 debut, through its controversial demolition, to today's reimagined forms.

name: Everything* AI Conference at Pioneer Works
why: AI conference at Pioneer Works with Paul Ford (Co-Founder, Aboard), Tido Carriero (VP Engineering, Cursor), David Crawshaw (Founder, Exe.dev), Andrew Qu (Chief of Software, Vercel), Magnus Hillestad (CEO, Sanity), and more tech founders. Free to attend.

name: AI Enterprise Conference at Pier Sixty
why: Enterprise AI conference at Pier Sixty with Michael Beal (Head of Enterprise Data Science, Bloomberg), Dhagash Mehta (Head of Applied ML, BlackRock), Joshua Ainsley (Head of Data Science, New Balance) — focused on enterprise data science and applied ML.

name: Fast Company Innovation Festival
why: Fast Company's annual Innovation Festival with Cristiano Amon (CEO, Qualcomm), Paul Dillinger (Head of Design Innovation, Levi Strauss), Mike Intrator (CEO, CoreWeave), and Rachel Kornafel (Chief Brand Officer, Union Square Hospitality).

name: Innovators Social at CUNY Advanced Science Research Center
why: Free innovators meetup hosted by ASRC CAT, Activate NY and HB at the CUNY Advanced Science Research Center in Harlem — connecting tech founders, investors, and researchers in science and innovation.

name: Arbrasson Instrument Workshop with Daniel Fishkin at Pioneer Works
why: Pioneer Works Artist-in-Residence Daniel Fishkin leads a hands-on workshop on the Arbrasson, a wooden friction idiophone from France — including a history/demo and a tutorial on building your own with a Ryoba saw and Kanna. $250 includes all materials.

name: 6A: Confinos Summer Tour at Tenement Museum (thru Aug 31)
why: Immersive tour featuring an actor as Victoria Confino, a Sephardic Jewish teenager who immigrated from Kastoria to the LES in 1913 — taking visitors into her family's recreated 1916 apartment and the summer rhythms of tenement life, from neighborhood ice cream to Coney Island.

name: Brooklyn Brainery September 2026 Classes — Watercolor, Tarot, Drawing, and More
why: Brooklyn Brainery's September lineup includes Watercolor Fundamentals, Classic Charcoal Drawing, Introduction to Gouache, Wet Felted Soaps, Tarot 101 and 201, Nonfiction Book Proposals, and more hands-on classes. Check the full schedule for dates.
